scope: Proposition 2.2 (A necessary normal polynomial) of the manuscript “Nagata's conjecture for plane curves” (preprints/Nagatas-Conjecture-for-Plane-Curves-September-23-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 039 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 42a8897d121e2fc0), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 4-5. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Suppose that Ur(d, m) holds. For every choice of distinct points a1, . . . , ar ∈ B and arbitrary vectors ci ∈ Mai , there is a nonzero polynomial F(w) = ⌊d/k⌋ X j=0 fjwj , fj ∈ H0 (B, Ld−kj ), (2.2) 4 having multiplicity at least m at each (ai, ci) ∈ Tot(M). Its coefficients may be taken to be algebraic sections.
